newsitem.title: INDIA: Morgan Stanley gives India message of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley gives India message of confidence.

text.p: Investment bank Morgan Stanley on Tuesday gave Indian corporate debt a "buy" rating and said it was issuing a "message of confidence" in the South Asian nation's economy.

Morgan Stanley said in a statement released in New Delhi that a recent assessment by U.S. credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service Inc, which had called India's creditworthiness unfavourable, was unduly harsh.

Earlier this month Moody's said India's unstable political environment, directionless economic policies and a deterioration in its macroeconomic balances had led it to take an unfavourable outlook on the nation's sovereign rating.
"In our view, this is an unduly harsh assessment of the country's creditworthiness," the statement quoted Morgan Stanley sovereign credit analyst Robert Smalley as saying.

Smalley said the Indian government's proposed budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1 represented "a plan to increase confidence and to spur growth -- not the stuff of a 'directionless' economic policy, as Moody's would have us believe".

Morgan Stanley said it believed credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp would look to upgrade India to BBB- from BB+ in the next 12 to 18 months. "We view the Republic of India as a stable low BBB credit," Smalley said.
